A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FOCAL research and contain complete, readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B. Corresponding content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, segmentation, pose-estimation, lighting, and active-vision experiments, including Figures 5–10 and appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical experiments and reports revised classification results in Tables 3 and 5.

M1.justification: The vary-and-rank procedure, CLIP and diffusion energies, transformation generation, and Bayesian optimization remain unchanged. Rewritten explanations do not establish an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same datasets and transformation tasks, including CIFAR10/100, STL10, ImageNet, Objaverse-LVIS, CO3D, COCO, RCC, KITTI-based day/night scenes, and eight active-vision scenes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments: PRLC, rotation augmentation, uncanonicalized and oracle models, TRELLIS, random rotations, TTA, and the RCC color-correction baselines remain.

E3.justification: Reported rotation protocols, metrics, model configurations, filtering, sample counts, and optimization budgets remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix B. The numerical revisions do not document changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: Figure 1 replaces the vase segmentation example with a person whose body parts are missed before canonicalization, revising the qualitative evidence illustrating rotation robustness. The systematic ablations, transfer analyses, TTA comparisons, and active-vision case study remain unchanged.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added or revised. Existing statistical reporting and plotted uncertainty displays are retained.

E6.justification: Tables 3 and 5 revise classification scores, oracle and uncanonicalized results, and gain annotations. For example, STL10 ResNet50 upright/rotated accuracy changes from 96.1/95.5 to 96.2/95.6, while FOCAL's ImageNet rotated ResNet50/ViT accuracy changes from 63.5/71.9 to 62.4/71.2. Figure 8 is updated, but the overall ordering against PRLC remains.

T1.justification: The invariance/equivariance definitions, energy equations, invertibility assumptions, and computational-cost derivation are retained. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical argument is added or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions claim training-free test-time canonicalization, approximate invariance across complex transformations, and improved downstream robustness and generalization. The rewritten abstract and introduction retain the same scientific contribution and scope.

C2.justification: The introduction changes photographer's bias from a proposed hypothesis for brittleness to an asserted partial cause. The substantive limitations concerning computation, transformation selection, noninvertible transformations, and color-correction performance remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Figure 1 newly specifies that its SAM example uses box prompting. Implementation settings in Appendix B, hardware and runtime reporting in Appendix A.10, and the code-access link are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Xiao et al. (2021), What Should Not Be Contrastive in Contrastive Learning, to support the discussion of over-regularization. It also explicitly distinguishes FOCAL's visual-typicality ranking from the previously cited test-time ranking work; the broader positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and most of the introduction are substantially rewritten and reorganized around human mental rotation and the contrast between training-time invariance and inference-time optimization. Smaller prose refinements occur elsewhere, while the method, experiment, and appendix section organization remains.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 replace illustrative examples, Figure 3 labels specific transformations, Figure 9 rearranges its panels, and Figure 10 clarifies its rows. Table 3 corrects best-score highlighting and uses red annotations for STL10 upright deficits. The overall figure/table inventory and layout are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies the opening narrative and correctly highlights rotation augmentation's superior STL10 upright scores in Table 3. However, Table 5 revisions introduce numerical inconsistencies: ViT rotated accuracy changes from 71.9% to 71.2%, while the stated +11.4-point gain and Appendix A.5's old value remain; 71.2 minus 60.5 is 10.7 points. These reporting problems offset presentation improvements enough that a reliable net quality judgment is unclear.
